rationale: Provisional recommendation: NO as of 2026-10-14. The official original is 83 FR 25329, PDF pages 1-6 (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2018-06-01/pdf/2018-11913.pdf, SHA-256 85bf124a5626c4e5bad111eb4ce5a882c81873fd2f85d12f30249ad8f33712be); all pages were inspected visually, including signature/closing page. The held official EO EO:14003 copy (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2021-01-27/pdf/2021-01924.pdf, SHA-256 d57516aba4a168838ff1efddd26cd84ead282fc8a1eff817e0c47db1d7866df0, 86 FR 7231, PDF pages 1-3) expressly revokes this target in section 3(a) and the instrument date is 2021-01-22; its specific effective-date clause is not separately explicit, so the legal-effective date remains unconfirmed. For EO 13836/13837/13839, a D.D.C. injunction dated 2018-08-25 barred enforcement of specified sections; the D.C. Circuit vacated that judgment and the 2019-10-11 Presidential Memorandum (84 FR 56095, GovInfo https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2019-10-21/pdf/2019-23021.pdf) says the mandate issued and clarifies treatment of CBAs executed during the injunction. This is a scoped temporary enforcement interruption, not a whole-order revocation. EO 14148 (2025-01-20; GovInfo PDF https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-28/pdf/2025-02006.pdf, SHA-256 d658f5158a27f6d4a220ce2ec854bdbd596ecc841fb16884954a2e2ee39ab072) expressly revokes EO 14003 and EO 14029 but does not name or reenact the four target orders. I do not infer revival from revocation of a later rescinding order; the 14148 language and an initial later-source scan support retaining NO, subject to bounded search and legal review. This remains a producer draft: no independent status review, no owner adoption, no complete clause first-ending proof, and residual savings/implementation effects remain open.
